item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mixed but leaning negative. Tshisekedi’s 2024 record includes some real crisis-response inputs, especially a solidarity cash allocation, stabilization programming, and support for ceasefire diplomacy. But the strongest evidence still shows mass displacement, acute hunger, underfunded humanitarian aid, and severe state-inflicted harm, so there is no good evidence of a durable reduction in avoidable suffering at scale.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Soirée de solidarité nationale](https://www.primature.gouv.cd/2024/02/16/soiree-de-solidarite-nationale-representant-le-president-de-la-republique-le-premier-ministre-sama-lukonde-remet-un-cheque-de-15-milliards-de-francs-congolais-aux-victimes-des-affres-de-guerres-et/) | Primature | 2024-02-16 | The government, on Tshisekedi’s behalf, allocated 15 billion CDF for victims of war, floods, landslides, and internal displacement. Real emergency relief, but small relative to the scale of need. | IDs: 6B.6
- [Programme de désarmement et démobilisation](https://acp.cd/nation/programme-de-desarmement-et-demobilisation-une-alternative-pour-la-paix-et-la-cohesion-sociale/) | ACP | 2024-03-22 | The administration framed P-DDRCS as a stabilization and cohesion program meant to restore state authority where absent. That is a plausible violence-reduction tool for conflict displacement, though still indirect evidence. | IDs: 6B.6
- [Collective effort essential to get DRC on firm path to peace](https://www.ungeneva.org/en/news-media/news/2024/09/98156/collective-effort-essential-get-dr-congo-firm-path-peace) | UN Office at Geneva | 2024-09-30 | The UN said fighting had decreased after the 30 July ceasefire and that a dialogue framework was active. That indicates at least temporary reduction in conflict-related suffering. | IDs: 6B.6
- [Democratic Republic of Congo Battling Worsening Humanitarian Crisis, Armed Conflict, Despite Recent Peaceful Elections](https://press.un.org/en/2024/sc15646.doc.htm) | UN Press | 2024-03-27 | The UN warned that eastern DRC’s humanitarian crisis was worsening and that roughly one in four Congolese faced hunger and malnutrition. This is strong negative evidence that avoidable suffering remained severe. | IDs: 6B.6
- [DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | Amnesty said there had been little to no progress, public resources were being squandered, and essential services were underfunded, leaving food, health, water, sanitation, education, and housing needs unmet. | IDs: 6B.6
- [DRC President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-30 | Amnesty said IDP camps remained dangerous, humanitarian aid was chronically underfunded, and the state of siege militarized daily life rather than protecting civilians. | IDs: 6B.6
- [World Report 2024: Democratic Republic of Congo](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | HRW said conflict caused mass displacement, disrupted humanitarian aid delivery, and produced food shortages in Goma, while Tshisekedi’s administration made little progress on systemic reform. | IDs: 6B.6
- [More than 260 women sexually assaulted during Congo prison break, UN reports shows](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/More-than-260-women-sexually-assaulted-during-Congo-prison-break-UN-reports-shows-47860482/) | Reuters | 2024-09-12 | Prison guards used live fire during the Makala escape attempt, killing at least 129 people and sexually assaulting more than 260 women. This is severe state failure to prevent avoidable suffering in custody. | IDs: 6B.6

**Search Gap**
- I found no 2024 independent dashboard, audit, or outcome study showing that Tshisekedi’s crisis interventions measurably reduced deaths, displacement, hunger, or service disruption.
- The positive evidence is mostly input-level or temporary, not proof of sustained humanitarian improvement.
